title: Lindy vs Metal: team credits or separate bots?
h1: lindy vs Metal: shared work, credits and control
description: Compare Lindy’s active-user pricing, pooled credits and scheduled routines with Metal’s separate bot roles, permissions and hosting costs.
answer: **lindy puts the helper where your team already talks. dusk gives each job its own home.** lindy handles email, meetings, leads and reports through tools such as slack and email.[^1] its team plan pools credits and charges per active user. dusk separates bot jobs, memory and ai choices, with ai usage and hosting billed separately.[^2][^5]
og_line: price the weekly job your team needs done.

them: **you want one hosted service for shared work.** reach it through slack, email and text.
**you prefer a team credit pool.** choose models within that service.
dusk: **you want distinct bot roles.** choose each bot’s ai and app permissions.
**you want to try jobs before choosing hosting.** start on your own computer and move later.

compare.h: how the assistant fits a working team
compare.intro: **price the routine your team will actually run.** monthly usd prices are as of 12 november 2026. lindy pools credits; how far they go depends on the work.

method:
**run the weekly report before betting the team’s workflow on it.** Metal is based on Dusk Bot. this compares the billing and features listed on 12 november 2026. we did not run matching tasks or measure credit use.

lindy’s integration count comes from lindy. we did not test every workflow or verify compliance claims. use the table to choose your trial and look at the actual output before committing.

sections.h: try the approval on a job with consequences
sections.md:
**find out where the bot stops before it touches a customer’s work.** lindy says actions with outside impact need approval.[^1] ask it to show that pause on the job your team needs.

in dusk, start with connected apps read only. for writes, say "ask me before you change anything". command and file approval levels are separate controls.[^9][^10]

then ask lindy what counts as an active user. [lindy alternatives](/alternatives/lindy) covers the credit pool and pricing in more detail.

faq.q: does lindy have a free plan?
faq.a: **you get a trial, not a renewing free allowance.** as of 12 november 2026, lindy lists $50 in credits for 7 days. team starts at $29.99 monthly per active user.[^2]
**yes, its pricing lists imessage.** it also lists slack, email and phone calls.[^2] dusk uses a paired phone browser today; store apps are still on the way.[^7]

faq.q: is lindy better than openclaw for a business owner?
faq.a: **pick who you want handling the upkeep first.** lindy is hosted; openclaw runs on your computer or server with no first-party hosted tier.[^1][^3] then try the same small job and compare the complete usage bill.

tip.text: ask what happens to unused credits. lindy’s pool does not roll over.
